fallback_summary_en: English often uses the preposition 'for' across relationships such as purpose, reason, destination, recipient, exchange, route, and target time. Other languages may divide those jobs among different grammatical forms.

transparency_slide.description: The lesson is declarative structure layered with language data. The app owns one universal lesson runner; lesson packages do not ship bespoke executable runners.
transparency_slide.rendering_model: Build one ordered language array from relevant profile/session languages. If that array contains no one-form profile, add English; if it contains no multi-form profile, add Spanish. Render every resulting entry with the same universal LanguageSample/LessonWordBrick component. English and Spanish are conditional contrast fallbacks, not permanently fixed first entries.

support_selection.full: Render the language comparison block plus structured GrammarRuleBlock sections and any defensible rule-driven practice.
support_selection.comparison_only: Render the language comparison block only. Do not synthesize missing grammar rules or practice.
support_selection.unavailable: Omit the language from this lesson.

title_policy.notes: The title is target/learning-language specific. Do not infer a universal one-word equivalent, and do not hand-concatenate translated words such as 'and' or commas.

eligibility.notes: The data model supports arbitrary language arrays. Twelve is only the default lesson-surface display cap; classroom/projector surfaces may raise it without changing the lesson schema. Intro contrast fallbacks are conditional: English supplies a one-form example only when needed, and Spanish supplies a multi-form example only when needed.

block_plan.notes: Show the dynamic target-language title and concise topic-specific description. Do not use a generic 'languages say things differently' lesson intro.

Resolve the display-ready deck from lessons/mul/multiple-words-for/word-examples.json. Begin with relevant profile/session languages, derive form counts from the forms array, inject English only when no one-form example is present, and inject Spanish only when no multi-form example is present.

Use the same ordered language set as the intro word examples. Full support may source structured grammar from Lexicon; comparison-only support uses the lightweight native-language comparison record. Do not add unconditional English/Spanish entries.

Explain relevant grammatical categories using selected full-support language metadata. Do not call every form a preposition; forms may be prepositions, postpositions, particles, case markers, clause markers, endings, or larger constructions.
Render universal GrammarRuleBlock components from structured Lexicon rule IDs. A global Tier 1/2 label alone never qualifies a language for this block.

Prefer exact approved handles from the current compatible text or the lesson-safe default corpus, including eligible Quotes Across the World anchors. LanguageSample is the universal presentation component and may also be used by books.
Friendly localized transition. Omit when selected learning languages have no defensible rule-driven practice.
Use shared practice primitives only where structured grammar records support a real decision. Wrong answers reveal the relevant rule/tips; no punitive streak behavior.
Teacher/session policy may hide, offer, or require a reader quest. Omit when selected learning languages have no meaningful target distinction.
Localized wrap-up and optional scorecard/celebration. Must work for comparison-only sessions with no quiz score.

learning_path_policy.notes: The same multilingual lesson family may appear at different positions in different language paths. Lesson-specific full support can be added for any global tier without changing that language's global tier.
